newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Sept ind. orders down, but revision likely.
newsitem.headline: German Sept ind. orders down, but revision likely.

text.p: German industry orders fell by 3.6 percent in September against August, data showed on Tuesday, but the Economics Ministry said it expected the figure to be revised upward later.
August orders figures were revised downward to show a month-on-month gain of 0.1 percent. The figures are seasonally adjused and expressed in volume terms.

The weak orders data followed data on Monday which also showed a slowdown in industrial output in September, but the ministry also expects that number to be revised up, based on historical experience.

The Federation of German Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) said in its autumn survey of 25,000 businesses that it expected the economy to grow by one percent this year and between 1.5 and two percent next year.
That is below forecasts by the Bonn government and leading German economic institutes of 2.5 percent growth next year.

Foreign orders, which have been leading Germany's moderate recovery, slowed by four percent in September against August. But in the latest two months foreign orders were still up by 6.6 percent on the same period a year earlier.
West German industry orders were down in September by 3.6 percent on the previous month, while in the former communist east orders were down by 2.6 percent.
